sections.title: Social Media *Strategy*
sections.subtitle: 10 ways to improve and grow Magus Fashion City's social media presence among garment manufacturers.

sections.title: Ten moves to make the page a *business hub*.

points.title: Position the page as a business hub, not a property ad
points.what: Give every post one of four jobs: proof, ecosystem, business know-how or product. Fix the bio, highlights and visual template to match.
points.why: A factory owner follows a page that helps his business. He scrolls past a page that only shows brochures and prices.
content: A monthly calendar built on the four pillars
Story highlights: Units, Ecosystem, Suvesha, Visit

points.title: Lead with proof: 940+ units already operating
points.what: Put existing unit owners on camera. Let them tell how the move changed their production, costs and orders.
points.why: The biggest doubt is whether a factory can run well in Bhiwandi. A fellow manufacturer answers that better than any ad.
content: Before and after the move stories

points.title: Show the real site every week
points.what: Shoot on site weekly and make video the main format. Use real footage of Suvesha and the park in place of renders.
points.why: A manufacturer checks floor space, lifts and truck access before he believes anything. Real video builds trust before the site visit.

points.title: Speak the trade's language: Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi
points.what: Make Hindi the main language for video. Add Gujarati and Marathi versions of the best posts. Use plain trade words.
points.why: Garment business in Mumbai is run in these languages. Content in the owner's own language is watched longer and shared more.

points.title: Teach first, sell second
points.what: Run a weekly know-how series on the problems owners face: finance, subsidies, compliance, labour and getting buyers.
points.why: Useful posts get saved and forwarded on WhatsApp. They also show that Magus understands the garment business.
content: Expert Q&A with the advisory team

points.title: Make content for each trade
points.what: Run one content series for each of the five segments: menswear, womenswear, ethnic wear, kidswear and bags.
points.why: A denim maker and a bag maker have different needs. An owner stops scrolling when he sees his own trade on screen.
content: A sample unit layout for each trade
Stories of owners from that trade

points.title: Give each platform one clear job
points.what: Stop posting the same creative everywhere. Set a role and a posting rhythm for each platform, about 4 to 5 posts a week in total.
points.why: Owners use each platform differently. Content made for the platform performs better than one post copied to all of them.

points.title: Turn events and trade shows into content
points.what: Cover every trade show, on-site exhibition and open day in three stages: before, during and after.
points.why: Events bring real crowds and real faces. Social media carries a one-day event to people who could not attend.
content: Recap video with a site visit offer

points.title: Build a community and reply fast
points.what: Feature the businesses inside the park and tag them. Answer every comment and message within one working hour.
points.why: Featured owners share the post with their own trade contacts, who are the exact audience. Fast replies turn questions into site visits.
content: Polls and question boxes in stories
Saved replies for price, size and location

points.title: Boost what works and measure enquiries, not likes
points.what: Put a small budget behind the best organic posts. Retarget people who watched the videos. Review results every month.
points.why: Organic reach alone is small. A post that already did well is a tested ad, so the money goes to proven content.
content: "Book a site visit" on every post

sections.ideasIntro: Suggested additions that turn existing owners, partners and everyday moments into enquiries.

ideas.title: Weekend site-visit shuttles
ideas.text: Free Saturday pickup from Mumbai's garment clusters to Bhiwandi, with a guided walkthrough and lunch. It removes the biggest barrier to a visit: the trip itself.

ideas.title: Refer-a-manufacturer rewards
ideas.text: 940+ operating units know other manufacturers. Reward owners and brokers for every referral that books a unit.

ideas.title: WhatsApp automation
ideas.text: Every lead from ads, the website or a QR scan lands in an automated WhatsApp flow: an instant brochure and walkthrough video, three qualifying questions, a site-visit slot picker and reminders. Hot leads go straight to sales, the rest get a weekly nurture message.

ideas.title: Webinars on investing & setting up a garment unit
ideas.text: Monthly online sessions: how to invest in industrial property and how to set up a garment business, with experts on finance, subsidies and operations. Each session ends with a Magus Fashion City walkthrough and an attendee-only offer, so every registration becomes a lead.

ideas.title: EMI vs rent calculator
ideas.text: An online calculator that compares the monthly EMI with current rent, then sends the full breakdown on WhatsApp. A lead magnet that also qualifies buyers.

ideas.title: SMS, RCS & email marketing
ideas.text: Low-cost reach to owners who are not on social media. SMS for short offers and site-visit invites, RCS for rich branded messages with images and a Book visit button, and email for brochures, floor plans and webinar invites.

ideas.title: Data buying for pre-sales & campaigns
ideas.text: Buy verified databases of garment manufacturers, traders, MSME owners and investors in Mumbai, Thane and Bhiwandi. The pre-sales team calls the best matches, and the same lists feed the SMS, RCS and email campaigns. Source only consented, DND-scrubbed data.

ideas.title: Hindi business creators
ideas.text: Sponsored walkthroughs with Hindi business and startup YouTubers who explain how to set up a garment unit.
